title: Tiered concession approval engine with usage-linked price bands
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request contract concessions (liability cap increases, indemnity carveouts, data residency assurances, audit windows) that require legal review and sometimes an elevated sales pricing conversation. Today these requests create long review cycles, inconsistent decisions across deals, and revenue leakage when sales over-discounts to close.

Goal: Build a deterministic, auditable 'concession approval engine' that maps common redlines to a risk score and to an automated approval path and (where appropriate) a recommended usage-linked price band. The engine should reduce manual legal review for low-to-medium risk concessions, provide a clear escalation path for high-risk asks, and surface the price delta required for accepting concessions so sales can close with transparent economics.

Scope: One quarter MVP covering the most frequent redlines identified by Legal and Sales: liability cap adjustments, indemnity narrowings (service-specific carveouts), DPA retention exceptions, subprocessing restrictions, and data-hosting region constraints. Integrate with Sales CRM (HubSpot/Salesforce), Legal intake (internal queue), and the Redwood Contract Generator UI. Deliverables: ruleset + scoring model, approval workflow UI in contract generator, autosuggested price-band, telemetry and decision ledger for audits, and doc links for legal rationale.

Out of scope for MVP: full free-form clause negotiation, escrow implementations, and bespoke escrow triggers (deferred to next phase).

Why now: Rising enterprise usage and larger commitments (Dedicated/Private) have increased both frequency and monetary impact of concession asks. A measurable reduction in time-to-decision and standardized pricing will improve close rates and reduce revenue write-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Policy/ruleset covering the 5 MVP concession types is defined and stored in a single source of truth (Confluence link attached)
Approval engine returns: risk score (none/low/medium/high), approval path (auto-approve / legal-review / C-level), and recommended price band (delta % or absolute) for test inputs
Sales UI surfaces suggested price delta and required approvers when generating an MSA/DPA amendment
Telemetry captures each decision: input flags, computed risk, approver decisions, final outcome, and time-to-decision
At least 40% of incoming MVP concession requests are auto-approved or routed to Sales Ops without legal review in pilot accounts
Decision ledger and rationale are exportable for audit and included in contract metadata stored with the executed agreement
comments: 2025-03-06 - Discovery: Interviewed Legal (Nina Martinez) and Sales Ops (Jordan Reed). Top friction: lack of clear pricing impact guidance and inconsistent territorial rules. Legal provided a list of 32 common redlines; we filtered down to top 5 for MVP.
2025-03-10 - Design sync: Drafted UI flow for Contract Generator; shows concession badge, suggested delta, and inline rationale. @Maya Patel (Design) will provide mockups by 2025-03-14.
2025-03-12 - Eng scoping: Backend estimate 5 points to implement rules engine + telemetry + CRM webhook. Integrations team flagged Salesforce field mapping as non-trivial; added dependency PM-712400.

2025-03-14 - Legal feedback: Proposed scoring thresholds reviewed. Legal pushed back on auto-approve for indemnity carveouts unless explicit customer insurance proof is provided. Action: add insurance-proof checkbox to input schema.

2025-03-16 - Risk trade-offs discussed: Conservative thresholds reduce time-to-close gains; more aggressive thresholds risk exposure. Decision: start conservative with explicit uplift recommendations; iterate with telemetry for loosening rules.

2025-03-18 - Pilot plan: Identify 3 customers in Dedicated pipeline for alpha pilot. Sales committed to using suggested band as a reference rather than override. Next: PRD finalization and engineering kickoff (target 2025-03-24).
notes: Design note: the UI should make it clear that suggested price bands are advisory for sales and binding once approved by the required approver levels.
Telemetry note: include tokenized link to contract version and commit hash for reproducibility of rationale at time of sign-off.
Follow-up: Evaluate automation of insurance validation via uploaded certificates in phase 2.
